subject: Marketplace addendum: risk mitigation & execution playbook
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@cloudsail.com>

Cc: David Rao <david.rao@cloudsail.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace addendum: pass-through & liability redlines

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is CloudSail's redline to the marketplace/reseller addendum (file: CloudSail_Addendum_redline_v2.docx). High-level asks from our legal and finance teams:

- Require pass-through of marketplace fees with explicit invoice owner mapping (orderform section 2.1).
- Seek a carveout limiting Redwood's indemnity exposure for downstream sellers (new section 5.4).
- Clarify audit rights and evidence scope — limit to 12-month trailing window and exclude customer PII logs.
- Add a standard escrow clause for disputed fees.

Can we set up a quick triage today or tomorrow? We have procurement review Friday and would like to lock on commercial flow and any non-negotiables.

Attaching the redline for your team to review. If there are items we think will need executive signoff or credits, flag them so we can move those through quickly.

Sara
Sara Li
Senior Counsel, Partnerships | CloudSail

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum: pass-through & liability redlines

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 9:12 AM Sara Li <sara.li@cloudsail.com> wrote:
> Vivek —
> Attached is CloudSail's redline ...

Thanks Sara — read through the redlines. Quick internal summary and recommended positions to accelerate: 

1) Pass-through invoicing (orderform mapping)
- Recommendation: Accept an explicit mapping table in the orderform that declares CloudSail as the invoice owner for marketplace fees; Redwood will provide token-level usage exports and a signed attestation of fee routing monthly. This keeps accounting clean and avoids revenue recognition disputes.

2) Indemnity and downstream seller carveout
- Recommendation: Propose narrow carveout language limited to third-party content claims where Redwood had no control and where CloudSail exercised sole responsibility for seller onboarding/verification. Do NOT accept broad seller indemnity shift. Suggest fallback: Redwood accepts indemnity for breaches caused by Redwood's runtime or model hosting only.

3) Audit/evidence scope
- Recommendation: Limit to 12-month trailing window (as requested) but add a mutual redaction clause for logs that include PII — ops will provide summarized telemetry and an attestation rather than raw logs. Also propose a pre-notice 10 business day window for on-site or forensic requests.

4) Escrow / disputed fee mechanism
- Recommendation: Agree in principle to hold disputed amounts in escrow but cap escrow to disputed invoiced amount and add a 60-day automatic release if there is no formal dispute resolution.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Legal (Karthik) to send proposed edits for the addendum by EOD tomorrow. (file: proposed_edits.docx)
- Revenue Ops (Marissa) to draft invoice ownership mapping and webhook spec by Wednesday.
- Partnerships (Vivek) to confirm triage time with CloudSail and escalate any credit ask.

If CloudSail confirms the mapping approach and the narrow indemnity carveout, we can close without executive signoff. Anything beyond that (e.g., unlimited escrow or a broad indemnity transfer) will need C-level approval.

-Karthik
Director, Partner Contracts | Redwood Inference

Vivek / Karthik — thanks for the quick read and the concrete recommendations.

We can take the proposed approach on invoicing mapping and the 12-month audit window with the PII redaction process. For indemnity: CloudSail will accept the narrower carveout you suggested (limited to Redwood-controlled runtime/model hosting).

On escrow: CloudSail is comfortable capping escrow to the disputed invoiced amount and a 60-day release. We will send an updated signable addendum after your proposed edits.

Let's lock the 3pm PT triage call. Agenda: confirm mapping table, agree final paragraph language for indemnity, and confirm escrow mechanics. I've shared a DocuSign envelope for signature after we align (link below).
